newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar slide reflects demand - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar slide reflects demand - central bank.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said a sharp slide in the Taiwan dollar's value on Monday reflected nothing more than market demand, noting that no speculation had been detected.

"The Taiwan dollar's movement simply reflects normal market demand," Tuan Chin-sheng, deputy director general of the central bank's foreign exchange department, told reporters after the market's close when asked to comment on the big downturn.
"We have not seen any speculation," Tuan added.
Tuan declined to comment further on the day's financial fireworks, which also included a stock market selloff that saw the Taiwan index tumble 3.72 percent to 7,966.64 points.

On Monday, the Taiwan dollar tumbled to its lowest close in nearly a year, as the politically inspired stock-market tumble triggered strong outflows of funds to better-performing markets overseas, dealers said.
The local unit sank steadly through the day, dipping as low as T$27.775 to the U.S. dollar before ending at T$27.759 against Saturday's T$27.660 close.
It was the Taiwan dollar's lowest close since a T$27.790 finish on June 8, 1996.
